title: Make service_type rate changes data-driven
body:
## Summary
- Add a `start_date` column to `service_type` so future rate changes are inserting a row, not editing code (the Fall 2023 change was fully manual — github.com/ctsit/rcc.billing/milestone/19).
- Add `get_effective_service_type()` to resolve the row effective per `service_type_code` as of a given date (latest `start_date <= as_of_date`, falling back to a `NULL`-start_date row).
- Wire it into `get_new_project_invoice_line_items()` (priced as of the invoicing date), `report/warn_owners_of_impending_bill.R` (priced as of next month, one month ahead of when the rate takes effect), and `report/warn_completers_of_impending_sequestration.R` (priced as of today) — all three previously used or hardcoded `$130`.
- `inst/schema/upgrade-1.54.0.sql` backfills `start_date = 2023-11-01` on the two existing rows and inserts the new **$150** annual-fee rate effective **2026-10-01**. Rename this file if the release it ships in ends up numbered differently.

`service_type_code = 2` (REDCap consulting) is unaffected — it isn't read by any script today.

## Test plan
- [x] `devtools::document()` — NAMESPACE/man updated
- [x] `devtools::test()` — 82/82 passing, including new tests for `get_effective_service_type()` and a before/after-2026-10-01 rate-switch test for `get_new_project_invoice_line_items()`
- [x] Manually linted the touched files against this repo's configured linters (`lintr::lint_package()` itself is currently broken here — pre-existing, unrelated `with_defaults()` removal in lintr 3.x)
- [x] DBA applies `inst/schema/upgrade-1.54.0.sql` against production when this ships

title: Revenue and receiveable report needs updates to probono work section
body:
The Revenue and receivables report needs updates to the pro bono work section. The report reads, "[Figure 5] shows the breakdown of Pro Bono costs by service type for the last fiscal year.", but that's not true. The report shows FY2024-2025 instead of FY2025-2026. We could solve this problem 1 of four ways:

1. Revise the report to show only FY2025-2026.
2. Revise the report to _dynamically_ select the fiscal year to display.
3. Show the data for all fiscal years from FY2024-2025 forward as they are completed.
4. Show the data for all fiscal years from FY2024-2025 forward with the current FY shown in its partial state.

As I write this, I prefer solution 4. I'm not sure this is the most useful solution, but it might be the least code. ;-)

title: Provide exceptions to the sequestration process for dormant projects
body:
We had a project get sequestered as "empty_and_inactive" because it was empty and inactive. Yet the PI wants it. they said,

> I open REDCap project PID 13172, and I am getting a notification that the project has been sequestered as of 03/01/2026 due to being empty and inactive. However, this project is still active. It has not been filled out recently by anyone showing interest in the study via the QR code it’s linked to which is simply due to not being contacted via this method, and it is empty because it is required for us to delete information from the forms once the person has been contacted, as they are entered into a separate project per our IRB protocol. Recruitment was simply separated from the main study REDCap project as a result of how the IRB required us to do things essentially. 

Indeed, the project is very inactive. See:
https://redcap.ctsi.ufl.edu/redcap/redcap_v16.1.4/Logging/index.php?pid=13172&usr=&record=&beginTime=&endTime=&dag=undefined&logtype=

The code tests last logged activity date on the project record. The test is, “is it more than a year old”. The relevant code is at https://github.com/ctsit/rcc.billing/blob/2b8556ad99a3ace45b29486b7b768711d64f4e26/R/get_orphaned_projects.R#L53

Curiously, the unsequestration process I bumped last logged activity today as I unsequestered the project.

title: Create a table `redcap_projects_history`

milestone.title: Describe Probono work
milestone.description: Create tables and reports needed to describe pro bono work. That will help us quantify the value of our work and our system in the places we do not charge court customers.

body:
Create a table in the `rcc_billing` database named `redcap_projects_history` to preserve the contents of every record in the `redcap_projects` table going forward. We will backfill the most critical facts about each fully deleted project using data from the `redcap_log_event*` tables. The backfill will allow essential queries.

For the mirroring, use 

```r
redcap_projects <- tbl(rc_conn, "redcap_projects") |> collect()
redcap_projects_history <- tbl(rc_billing_conn, "redcap_projects_history") |> collect()

redcapcustodian::sync_table_2(
  conn = rc_billing_conn,
  table_name = "redcap_projects_history",
  source = redcap_projects,
  source_pk = "project_id",
  target = redcap_projects_history,
  target_pk = "project_id",
  insert = T,
  update = T,
  delete = F
)
```

The script created needs to be fully automated and run once per day.

## Backfilling

After the initial mirror operation builds the table, we need to backfill the table with rows about deleted projects. Get the project lifecycle history like this. It takes about 90 seconds to query all the log_event tables:

```r
rc_conn <- connect_to_redcap_db()

creation_data_from_redcap_projects <- tbl(rc_conn, "redcap_projects") %>%
  select(project_id, creation_time) |>
  collect()

system.time(
  project_life_cycle <- get_project_life_cycle(rc_conn)
)
```

Make the dataset we'd like to backfill into redcap_projects_history

```r
creation_and_deletion_facts <- project_life_cycle |>
  # narrow our focus
  select(project_id, ts, description) |>
  # annotate the log rows
  group_by(project_id) |>
  mutate(field_name = case_when(
    str_detect(description, "^Create project") ~ "creation_time",
    str_detect(description, "^Copy project from") ~ "creation_time",
    str_detect(description, "^Copy project$") ~ "creation_time",
    str_detect(description, "^(D|d)elete project$") ~ "date_deleted"
  )) |>
  ungroup() |>
  # get rid of duplicate deletion events
  mutate(description = if_else(str_detect(description, "^delete project$"), "Delete project", description)) |>
  arrange(desc(ts)) |>
  distinct(project_id, description, .keep_all = T) |>
  # get rid of rows that do not describe the events of interest
  filter(!is.na(field_name)) |>
  # Make a timestamp for the event
  mutate(value = ymd_hms(ts)) |>
  select(-ts) |>
  # Pivot to the shape of redcap_projects
  pivot_wider(
    id_cols = "project_id",
    names_from = "field_name",
    values_from = "value"
  ) |>
  # Ensure we have every possible creation date by getting the ones we know from redcap_projects
  left_join(creation_data_from_redcap_projects, by = "project_id") |>
  mutate(creation_time = coalesce(creation_time.y, creation_time.x)) |>
  # Fill in missing creation dates
  arrange(project_id) |>
  fill(creation_time, .direction = "downup") |>
  # Keep only the columns in redcap_projects
  select("project_id", "creation_time", "date_deleted")
```

Sync this to the history table:

```r
redcap_projects_history <- tbl(rc_billing_conn, "redcap_projects_history") |> collect()

redcapcustodian::sync_table_2(
  conn = rc_billing_conn,
  table_name = "redcap_projects_history",
  source = creation_and_deletion_facts,
  source_pk = "project_id",
  target = redcap_projects_history,
  target_pk = "project_id",
  insert = T,
  update = T,
  delete = F
)
```

You should only need to do this once, but save the complete script into `./etl/run_once/`

title: Describe probono work in a report

milestone.title: Describe Probono work
milestone.description: Create tables and reports needed to describe pro bono work. That will help us quantify the value of our work and our system in the places we do not charge court customers.

body:
Update [revenue_status_and_projections.qmd](https://github.com/ctsit/rcc.billing/blob/main/report/revenue_status_and_projections.qmd) to describe probono work. Quantify probono from both the support billing and from annual project billing.

## Support billing

To quantify probono support billing, get the number of hours on each PB transaction with a query like this:

```sql
SELECT id, qty_provided, fiscal_year, month_invoiced, created
 FROM invoice_line_item
where 
service_type_code = 2
and price_of_service = 0
```

To turn the hours into a dollar figure, get the relevant rate in each `fiscal_year, month_invoiced` combination with a query like this:

```r
normal_service_rate <- tbl(rcc_billing_conn, "invoice_line_item") |>
  select(fiscal_year, month_invoiced, price_of_service) |>
  group_by(fiscal_year, month_invoiced, price_of_service) |>
  count(fiscal_year, month_invoiced, price_of_service) |>
  ungroup() |>
  collect() |>
  mutate(old_order = row_number()) |>
  arrange(desc(n)) |>
  distinct(fiscal_year, month_invoiced, .keep_all = T) |>
  arrange(old_order) |>
  select(-c(old_order, n))
```

Combine these data and compute a line item cost from the hours and price. Create a data frame with line-item detail. The columns output should be 

```
fiscal_year, month_invoiced, value
```

We'll summarize it to the granularity we need later. 

## Annual Project Billing (APB)

Compute the annual project billing revenue we give away by computing the days between the project deletion and the previous project anniversary. These dates are hard to come by for deleted projects we never invoiced, so we'll make a data source to preserve project history in another table. Let's call that data source `redcap_projects_history`. The construction of that table is described in Issue #270.

The probono APB service for one project will be `(date_deleted - creation_time) * normal_service_rate$price_of_service` where `price_of_service` is in the month the project was deleted. We will produce this number for all projects deleted on or after 2022-09-07, the day after we ran the first `warn_owners_of_impending_bill` job. Yet we will only do this for projects with `billable == 1`. You can get the billable column from `redcapcustodian::get_project_details_for_billing()`

Use the deletion date to compute the columns `fiscal_year` and `month_invoiced`. Steal code from https://github.com/ctsit/rcc.billing/blob/64a993200551a42e7cb44bed384e531422feb49d/etl/create_and_send_new_invoice_line_items.R#L124 to compute the fiscal year. Set the month_invoiced to the deletion month.

As above, the output data frame should have these columns:

```
fiscal_year, month_invoiced, value
```

## Combining the data

Bind the rows of the two data frames of support billing and annual project billing data. As you do, add a column `revenue_source` that indicates which dataset provided the revenue.

## Visualization

Add a "Pro Bono work" section before the "Aging Report" section. Place this text immediately after the "Pro Bono work" heading:

> CTS-IT does not charge for all its services. It offers a free consultation of up to an hour for every REDCap project on the CTSI REDCap system. This allows our customers to get free REDCap expertise as they plan their data collection efforts. Similarly, CTS-IT forgives up to a year of charges for every REDCap project if the owner deletes it before the next invoicing. This allows study teams to learn REDCap for free, taking tutorials, building projects, testing designs, and building the data collection instruments they will ultimately use in their study. Studies can be built, deployed, and completed entirely free of charge if done in under one year. 
> 
> Table NN shows the value of these services by fiscal year since CTS-IT started carefully accounting for charged and non-charged services. Figure MM shows the monthly detail underlying the annual figures. Support billing started 21 months after the annual project billing.


Show a summary table showing pro bono value by FY. Include a column for the revenue by fiscal year as is shown in Figure 3 of the report.  Include a column "Pro Bono services as a portion of revenue" that is the pro bono value / revenue. Format this column as a percentage with no decimal places. The column order should be FY, Revenue, "Value of Pro Bono Services", "Pro Bono Services as a portion of revenue".

Add a faceted plot with one facet per category, showing each source's pro bono value over time by month in a bar chart. Make each facet look like Figure 2, "REDCap APB Revenue generated by the month in which the journal entry was posted."

title: Allow support billing to include records with no project_id
body:
Allow support billing to include records with no project_id. 

## Background

The initial designs for REDCap Support Billing included the ability to charge for support requests not associated with a project. @pbchase omitted non-project-related requests in the first support billing release because of lack of time. That omission excluded these request types we never wanted to bill for:

- 1 | Account unsuspension
- 2 | Quote for a grant application
- 3 | Project un-sequestration
- 4 | Software bug report
- 6 | Politics
- 7 | Request took less than a minute to complete.

Yet, we need to bill for some requests unrelated to a specific project. @tlstoffs is presenting an all-day REDCap training session to customers willing to pay for her skills so they can level up theirs. @pbchase would like to log non-REDCap tasks in the same support database to exploit the automated billing workflows. 

## Implementation

To bill for projects without PIDs, we must remove the `project_id` requirement at line 25 in [get_service_request_lines()](https://github.com/ctsit/rcc.billing/blob/e627d218720ce1edb9e1162eb59ad8c4630a2c5d/R/get_service_request_lines.R#L25) and exclude the above request types. We don't want to mark those service request types as pro-Bono, as it would require a lot of work for the fiscal staff while never generating revenue.

`delete_abandoned_projects.R` needs to test the current sequestration state. As documented in issue #254, the test for `sequestered_orphans` is too simplistic at
https://github.com/ctsit/rcc.billing/blob/4b94e38f6bacbea69e65cd7d66d6e70167624519/etl/delete_abandoned_projects.R#L37

That is a test for projects that _were_ sequestered. The code should also test those projects _are still_ sequestered.  

You could fix that by adding this object

```
is_sequestered <- tbl(rc_conn, "redcap_projects") |>
  left_join(tbl(rc_conn, "redcap_entity_project_ownership"), by = c("project_id" = "pid")) |>
  filter(!is.na(completed_time) & sequestered == 1) |>
  select(project_id)|>

```

And using it to filter `sequestered_orphans`

title: PID 7022 is repeatedly deleted

milestone.title: Stop deleting formerly sequestered projects

body:
@tlstoffs reports the project with [PID 7022](https://redcap.ctsi.ufl.edu/redcap/redcap_v14.7.2/index.php?pid=7022) is repeatedly deleted. The deletion is not being logged. @tlstoffs saw the sequestered flag was on. She unchecked that flag.

## Background and research

I think this was caused by an rcc.billing script. The script that does that is `delete_abandoned_projects`. To verify that, I explored the rcc job log. I used this code:

```
library(redcapcustodian)
library(rcc.billing)
library(RMariaDB)
library(DBI)
library(tidyverse)
library(lubridate)
library(dotenv)
library(fs)

load_dot_env("prod.env")

init_etl("pbc_scratch")
rc_conn <- connect_to_redcap_db()
log_conn <- get_package_scope_var("log_con")

log_data <-
  tbl(log_conn, "rcc_job_log") %>%
  dplyr::filter(script_name == "delete_abandoned_projects") %>%
  arrange(desc(id)) |>
  collect()

log_data |>
  filter(str_detect(job_summary_data, "7022")) |>
  unnest_job_summary_data_json_object() |>
  filter(pid == 7022)
```

It showed

```
    id  pid           reason  status            log_date     project instance               script_name     script_run_time job_duration   level
1 2418 7022 orphaned project deleted 2024-07-28 18:03:04 rcc.billing     prod delete_abandoned_projects 2024-07-28 18:03:03     1.168833 SUCCESS
2 2140 7022 orphaned project deleted 2024-06-28 18:03:43 rcc.billing     prod delete_abandoned_projects 2024-06-28 18:03:42     1.137561 SUCCESS
```

This additional code provided a long, history with less detail:

```
tbl(log_conn, "rcc_job_log") %>%
  # count(script_name)
  arrange(desc(id)) |>
  collect() |>
  filter(str_detect(job_summary_data, "7022"))
```

## The bug in `delete_abandoned_projects`

So `delete_abandoned_projects` thinks the project was orphaned. Reviewing the logs and the code, I can see 7022 was sequestered 2023-06-01. Yet it was not sequestered when it was deleted. `delete_abandoned_projects` does not test that a project _is_ sequestered, only that it _was_ sequestered 12-14 months earlier. It needs the additional test that a project _is_ sequestered. 

## Why were the deletions not logged?

The project deletions are not visible in the REDCap UI. They are in the table because `redcapcustodian::delete_project()` inserts a record into the log table, but it does a poor job. That function needs an update to accurately log a project deletion record.

title: Move test data 1
body:
@saipavan10-git, I started a project last night to move test functions and test data into the `./tests/testthat/` space. The commits in this PR are the first of many. I'll admit I might merge this and release it because I want to see the documentation changes reflected in the public documentation website. Yet I want you to see what I am doing. It's a multi-pronged effort to reduce the scope of what is documented so you and others are not distracted by test code and test data.  The changes come in a few forms:

## Testing helpers

I moved several testing helper functions from `R/devtools.R` to `tests/testthat/helper-package-specific.R`. Files that match the pattern `tests/testthat/helper*.R` are executed before running tests. It makes the functions available to tests and only tests.

Moving the functions makes their man pages disappear from `./man/`

## Moving test data
We generated a lot of test data with code in `./data-raw/`, writing the test data to `./data/`, and documenting it with Roxygen2 code in `./R/data.R`. All that was the wrong approach. To fix that, I am making these changes:

- I am moving test data from `./data/foo_test_data.rd?` to `./tests/testthat/foo/test_data.rd?` or `./tests/testthat/foo/foo_test_data.rd?`
- I am moving the code that generated the test data from `./data-raw/foo_test_data.R` to `./tests/testthat/foo/make_test_data.R`. In the same stroke, I change the place where `make_test_data.R` writes its output.
- I am deleting the docs for the test data sets from `./R/data.R`. That deletion makes their  man pages disappear from `./man/`

## Replacing SQLite3 with DuckDB

In older tests, we use in-memory SQLite3 databases to house test data when tests need to run a function that connects to a DB. This was a poor choice because the SQLite3 data types are so limited. The lack of a proper datetime format is a big issue. In modern tests, we use a DuckDB in-memory database for its richer datatype support. In these commits, I am replacing SQLite use with Duck DB. 

## Streamlined table creation

In the older tests, we would create a table from a schema file, then populate the table from a test dataset. In newer tests, we create and populate tables in one step by reading a dataframe of test data, then calling with `DBI::dbWriteTable()` with the data frame as the `value` option to  `DBI::dbWriteTable()`

## Stop testing Schema files

We have a few tests of schema files to verify they load correctly. They are hacky, nearly useless, and a pain to rework for DuckDB. I am deleting these tests.

## Other stuff

I have had to make a few small tweaks to functions and tests that broke with DuckDB, but they are few in number and small in size.

title: Revise `get_new_project_invoice_line_items` to use organizational data

milestone.title: Charge external customers a different rate

body:
Revise `get_new_project_invoice_line_items` (See PR #230) to use organizational data to determine if we should charge DSO Shands customers the $215, external non-profit rate.

`ctsi_rcc_billing.org_hierarchies` will tell you DEPT_IDs have `string::str_detect(dept_name, "DSO-SHANDS")`. `ctsi_rcc_billing.person_org` will tell you which people are in which organization. The orgs of interest all have this pattern:

```sql
SELECT * FROM org_hierarchies
where
DEPT_ID like '9501%';
```

So you can filter for people that work for UF Health Shands like this:

```sql
SELECT * FROM ctsi_rcc_billing.person_org
where
primary_uf_fiscal_org like '9501%';
```

Any PI/Owner who has `stringr::str_starts(primary_uf_fiscal_org, "9501")` should be charged the $215/hour (or $215/project) rate

title: Write a function, `get_ctsi_study_id_to_project_id_map()`

milestone.title: Design and build a support billing process
milestone.description: Design and build a support billing process

body:
Write a function, `get_ctsi_study_id_to_project_id_map()`. This function should read invoice line item records and service_requests to get unique, modern CTSI Study IDs for each REDCap Project. 

Require a parameter, `service_requests` containing some subset (all??) of the records and columns read from PID 1414.
Require a parameter, `rc_billing_conn`, a DBI connection object to an rcc.billing database containing an `invoice_line_items` table.

```r
# Read invoice line item records
extant_invoice_line_items <- tbl(rc_billing_conn, "invoice_line_item") |>
  collect()

# Get unique, modern CTSI Study IDs for each REDCap Project
# Get them from extant_invoice_line_items. We need both the annual project
# billing line items and the service_request  line items. 
# We have to join the latter to the service request history to map
# service_request line items to the PIDs they relate to. 
result <-
  bind_rows(
    extant_invoice_line_items |>
      filter(service_type_code == 1 & !is.na(ctsi_study_id)) |>
      arrange(desc(id)) |>
      select(id, service_type_code, service_identifier, ctsi_study_id) |>
      rename(project_id = service_identifier),
    extant_invoice_line_items |>
      filter(service_type_code == 2 & !is.na(ctsi_study_id)) |>
      arrange(desc(id)) |>
      select(id, service_type_code, service_identifier, ctsi_study_id) |>
      inner_join(service_requests |> select(record_id, project_id),
        by = c("service_identifier" = "record_id")
      ) |>
      select(service_type_code, project_id, ctsi_study_id)
  ) |>
  arrange(desc(id)) |>
  distinct(project_id, ctsi_study_id)

return(result)
```

title: Mark pro-bono service request records

milestone.title: Design and build a support billing process
milestone.description: Design and build a support billing process

body:
Create an ETL to mark records as pro-bono. This script will run every two hours from 7 a.m. - 9 p.m. name the etl `update_probono_service_request_records` or something better if you can thing of one.

```r

# Convert this code block into a function named get_probono_service_request_updates() or some such
# Add a test for this function. 
probono_updates <- service_requests |>
  arrange(record_id, redcap_repeat_instrument, redcap_repeat_instance) |>
  # fill project ids on each record group
  group(record_id) |>
  fill(project_id, .direction = "updown") |>
  ungroup() |>
  filter(!is.na(project_id)) |>
  # Compute time, and time total for each project_id-probono group
  mutate(time = service_request_time(time2, time_more)) |>
  mutate(probono = (billable_rate == 0)) |>
  select(
    record_id,
    redcap_repeat_instrument,
    redcap_repeat_instance,
    project_id,
    probono,
    time,
    billable_rate
    ) |>
  group_by(project_id, probono) |>
  mutate(total_time = sum(time)) |>
  ungroup() |>
  # Copy probono time to each record across a project_id group
  group(project_id) |>
  mutate(probono_time = case_when(
    probono ~ total_time,
    TRUE ~ 0
  )) |>
  mutate(probono_time = max(probono_time)) |>
  # Mark additional records as probono as needed
  filter(probono_time < 1) |>
  arrange(time) |>
  mutate(additional_time = cumsum(time)) |>
  filter(additional_time + probono_time >= 1) |>
  filter(additional_time == min(additional_time)) |>
  mutate(billable_rate = 0) |>
  ungroup() |>
  # keep only enough columns to update the service request DB
  select(
    record_id,
    redcap_repeat_instrument,
    redcap_repeat_instance,
    billable_rate
  )

# update the service request DB
# Log the changes
```

title: Create service_request_time()

milestone.title: Design and build a support billing process
milestone.description: Design and build a support billing process

body:
Create this function

```r
service_request_time <- function(time_minutes, time_hours) {
  result <- tibble(
    time_minutes = time_minutes,
    time_hours = time_hours
    ) |>
    mutate(time = case_when(
      time_minutes %in% c(15,30,45,60) ~ time_minutes/60,
      time_hours > 1 ~ time_hours,
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    )) |>
    pull(time)
  
  return(result)
}
```

Add documentation. Include an example that looks kind of like the test code below. Make sure it passes the build check.

Make a test for it that looks kind of like this:

  7, 75, 1.75, 1.75
) |>

title: Write a function `get_service_request_lines()`

milestone.title: Design and build a support billing process
milestone.description: Design and build a support billing process

body:
Write a function `get_service_request_lines()`. This function will query Taryn's Service Request project to find completed, billable items.  This process requires data from:

- [REDCap Service Request](https://redcap.ctsi.ufl.edu/redcap/redcap_v14.2.0/index.php?pid=1414)
- rcc.billing.invoice_line_items

The function should have these features:

## Params

1. Require a parameter, `service_requests` containing a subset of the records and a subset of the columns read from PID 1414.

## Get service request details

```r
request_details <- service_requests |>
  filter(is.na(redcap_repeat_instrument)) |>
  # Filter for completed service requests. 
  # How do I know this????
  mutate(service_identifier = paste(record_id)) |>
  mutate(service_type_code = 2) |>
  mutate(service_instance_id = paste(service_type_code, service_identifier, sep = "-")) |>
  mutate(username = coalesce(redcap_username, gatorlink)) |>
  separate_wider_delim(pi, delim = " ", names = c("pi_fn", "pi_ln")) |>
  mutate(
    pi_last_name = coalesce(pi_ln, last_name),
    pi_first_name = coalesce(pi_fn, first_name),
    pi_email = coalesce(pi_email, email)
  ) |>
  select(record_id, project_id, irb_number, submit_date, username, pi_last_name, pi_first_name, pi_email)
```

## get service response details

```r
response_details <- service_requests |>
  filter(!is.na(redcap_repeat_instrument)) |>
  # Filter for completed service requests. 
  # How do I know this????
  filter(!is.na(billable_rate)) |>
  mutate(probono = (billable_rate == 0)) |>
  rename(price_of_service = billable_rate) |>
  group_by(record_id, probono, price_of_service) |>
  mutate(time = service_request_time(time2, time_more)) |>
  summarize(qty_provided = sum(time), response = paste(response, collapse = " ")) |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(amount_due = price_of_service * qty_provided)
```

## join responses and requests

```r
request_lines <- request_details |>
  inner_join(response_details, by="record_id") |>
  mutate(service_instance_id = if_else(
    probono, 
    paste0(service_instance_id, "-PB"), 
    service_instance_id)) |>
  mutate(
    other_system_invoicing_comments =
      str_trim(
      str_sub(
        paste0(
          service_identifier,
          username,
          submit_date,
          if_else(probono, paste0("Pro-bono : ", response), response),
          sep = " : "
        ),
        1, 255
      )
      )
  ) |>
  select(
    record_id,
    project_id,
    service_identifier,
    service_type_code,
    service_instance_id,
    irb_number,
    pi_last_name,
    pi_first_name,
    pi_email,
    other_system_invoicing_comments,
    qty_provided,
    amount_due,
    price_of_service
  )
```

- project_id
- app_title
- billable
- sequestered
- creation_time
- pi_last_name = coalesce(user_lastname, project_pi_lastname, lastname),
- pi_first_name = coalesce(user_firstname, project_pi_firstname, firstname),

- ctsi_study_id (or should something else fetch this? it is available in the REDCap DB because `invoice_line_item` is synch'd by `update_invoice_line_items_with_invoicing_details.R`)

Steal code from [create_and_send_new_redcap_prod_per_project_line_items.R](https://github.com/ctsit/rcc.billing/blob/5c8c4ea781d77bbf9eefcbbe583633f01c32f8c4/etl/create_and_send_new_redcap_prod_per_project_line_items.R#L74), line 74-119, but edit out all of the filters.

To do this, the code will need data from these tables:

- redcap.redcap_projects
- redcap.redcap_entity_project_ownership
- redcap.redcap_user_information
- redcap.invoice_line_item

body:
Write a function `create_service_request_line_items()`. This function assembles parts of the service request, project details, and line item history to make a whole line item.

## Params

1. Require a parameter, `service_requests` containing some subset of the records and columns read from PID 1414.
2. Require a parameter, `rc_billing_conn`, a DBI connection object to an rcc.billing database containing an `invoice_line_items` table.

## Get the dependencies

Call these functions:

- `get_service_request_lines()` - from Issue #205
- `get_ctsi_study_id_to_project_id_map()` - from Issue #208
- `get_project_details_for_billing()` - from Issue #204

Join the above data and select the fields needed to create an invoice_line_item_record. Where variables are in conflict, prefer the fact from `get_service_request_lines()`. This will happen with PI and IRB details. `coalesce()` each of these pairs and list the column from `get_service_request_lines()` first. @tlstoffs and @pbchase discussed this detail and decided we should honor the service request.

This function cannot know the ID of these rows until it inserted, so _do not set the ID in this function_. ID will be set at insertion by the script that calls this function.

Return the result.

title: Fix crashes in sequester_unpaid_projects.R
body:
Apologies for the very large commit. It should have been two commits. i.e., these fixes:

- Move single named columns from collect() to pull() in sequester_unpaid_projects.R. 
- Convert project_ids_to_sequester to numeric to prevent errors in sequester_projects().
- Shorten completed_by and truncate it to 100 characters to prevent crashes on during MySQL write in sequester_projects(). 
- Remove commented code from sequester_projects().

...followed by this massive refactor:

- Move sequester_projects() and get_orphaned_projects() to their own files. 
- Move sequester_projects() and get_orphaned_projects() tests to their own files. 
- Replace sequester_projects() tests with the modern model:
-   Put test data generation code and test data under tests/testthat/sequester_projects/
-   Write and read test data to individual rds files with purrr
-   Use DuckDB for the testing DB.
- Add create_a_table_from_rds for more streamlined test table management.

Sadly the massive refactor makes it hard to see how few changes I made to sequester_projects() as I moved it to a new file.

All that said, the bug fixes are boring. The hotness is in the test code. Specifically...

1. the addition of `create_a_table_from_rds()`
2. using the more modern test data model in `tests/testthat/sequester_projects/`
3. using the more modern Duck DB
4. and the vastly streamlined test at `tests/testthat/test-sequester_projects.R` the new model and create_a_table_from_rds() allow. 

I love using purrr::walk to generate and rds files. :-)
